about.title: About Me
paragraphs: I am an M.S. student in Applied Mathematics and Statistics at Johns Hopkins University and a visiting graduate student in Biostatistics at Harvard. My research focuses on AI for biology, supported by a background in mathematics and statistics.
I study scaling laws for single-cell representation models, examining how cell number, sequencing depth, and batch structure shape biological information recovery and experimental design.

I also build pipelines that connect cellular representations with large language models for cell-to-text generation and interpretation. I am interested in extending this work to multimodal foundation models for biology.

items.institution: Broad institute of Harvard of MIT
items.topic: Pathway-Independent Genetic Signals in Type 2 Diabetes Clusters
bullets: Investigating whether data-driven genetic clusters in type 2 diabetes capture biological information beyond curated pathway-based polygenic scores.
Constructing individual-level cluster-specific scores from variant-level disease clusters and comparing them with pathway-based pPGS derived from Reactome and KEGG.
Studying whether residual cluster signals can reveal novel or cross-pathway disease mechanisms.

items.institution: Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health
items.topic: Scaling Laws in Single-Cell Representation Learning
bullets: Applying Random Matrix Theory to derive mutual-information-based measures for biological signal recovery in single-cell multi-omics data.
Developing theoretical scaling laws for cell number, sequencing depth, and batch effects in single-cell data.
Conducting real-data analyses to evaluate how representation learning embeddings recover biological information.

items.topic: Survival Analysis in Oncology Clinical Trials
bullets: Performed survival analysis on multi-arm oncology clinical trial data.
Constructed time-to-event endpoints for staggered therapy initiation, treatment discontinuation, and right-censoring.
Conducted Kaplan-Meier analysis, median survival estimation, and Cox proportional hazards modeling with clinical covariates.

items.institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
items.topic: Single-Cell Sequencing Analysis of Blood Tissue Samples
bullets: Analyzed single-cell sequencing data from blood tissue samples to study cellular-level molecular profiles.
Used PCA and Leiden clustering to identify heterogeneous cell populations and annotate cells with marker genes.
Applied cellular enrichment analysis to connect marker genes with disease-related biological signals.

paper.title: Random Matrix Scaling Laws in Single-Cell Representation Learning
paper.authors: Sijia Zhu, Jingyuan Hu, Gokul Gowri, Allon M. Klein*, and Rong Ma**
paragraphs: This work studies how cell number, sequencing depth, and batch structure shape biological information recovery in single-cell representation learning. It connects a random matrix theory framework with empirical evaluation of single-cell representations, including scVI, Geneformer, and scGPT.

A further focus is experimental design under fixed budgets: how to balance cell number and sequencing depth when collecting single-cell data. Applications include systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) and Perturb-seq datasets.
